{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Ship Canal Bridge is a double-deck steel truss bridge that carries Interstate 5 (I-5) over Seattle's Portage Bay (part of the Lake Washington Ship Canal, after which it is named) between Capitol Hill and the University District.","title":"Ship Canal Bridge"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The canal below connects Lake Union with Lake Washington.","title":"Ship Canal Bridge"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Construction was completed in 1961 and the bridge opened to traffic on December 18, 1962.","title":"Ship Canal Bridge"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" It is 4,429 ft (1,350 meters) long, stands 182 feet above the canal and is 119 feet wide at the upper deck.","title":"Ship Canal Bridge"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" It was the largest bridge of its kind in the Northwest when it first opened.","title":"Ship Canal Bridge"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" The bridge is double-decked, with the upper deck carrying traffic in both directions and the lower deck (the express lanes) carrying traffic southbound in the morning and northbound in the afternoon.","title":"Ship Canal Bridge"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Fremont Cut is a body of water that forms part of the Lake Washington Ship Canal, which passes through the U.S. city of Seattle and links Lake Washington to Puget Sound.","title":"Fremont Cut"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The Fremont Cut connects Lake Union to the east with Salmon Bay to the west.","title":"Fremont Cut"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" It is 5800 ft long and 270 ft wide.","title":"Fremont Cut"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The center channel is 100 ft wide and 30 ft deep.","title":"Fremont Cut"}],"peer_messages":["Unverified peer answer: noanswer","Unverified peer answer: noanswer"],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"On which coast can the California Aqueduct and the Lake Washington Ship Canal be found?
